title: MTNL: A Unified Modeling Perspective for Enhancing Tensor Network Learning
claim: Prior single-purpose models are generalized into a unified multi-component framework that gains expressiveness, flexibility and efficiency from complementary parts.
layout: 3 dashed panels, left-to-right, top arrow linking baseline to unified framework
description: A wide figure with a top banner arrow labeled 'Generalization with Enhancement' leading from 'Tensor Network Learning' to 'Mixed Tensor Network Learning (MTNL)'. The left dashed panel shows the standard Input→TN-Model→Output setup with two examples: tensor recovery (a table feeding a blue triangle node graph into a cube with a question mark) and model compression (image→feed-forward→TN→feed-forward→Cat/Dog). The center panel shows several blue and green triangle-shaped tensor networks combined by plus and nonlinearity nodes in a deep-network style, with width and depth dashed boxes, labeled Expressiveness. Below it a second panel covers the flexible TN structure-search prior, a marginal-distribution plot and sparsity reweighting scales, labeled Flexibility. The right panel contrasts existing uncertainty quantification, which needs complex contraction and extensive sampling, with the MTNL-Dropout approach, labeled Efficiency. Orange labels mark the three benefits.
caption: The overall structure of MTNL.
abstract: Over the years, the unsupervised and supervised learning research directions of tensor networks (TNs) have mainly developed in parallel. In this paper, we provide a view for their cooperative advancement through a novel mixed tensor network learning (MTNL) framework that unifies the two fields. Specifically, inspired by supervised TN learning tasks, multiple TNs are fused in a deep-network style in MTNL, enhancing the expressive power for the unsupervised TN learning tasks. We then develop a more flexible TN structure search prior with theoretical guarantees for learning multiple TN structures, aligning with trends in many supervised learning setups. More interestingly, by combining these components within a Bayesian framework, we show that MTNL induces a lightweight uncertainty quantification mechanism that is theoretically guaranteed by its connection to the dropout-based counterpart problem, making the mechanism a potential alternative for large-scale learning problems. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the MTNL framework on tensor recovery, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and tensor regression experiments.
